question: When was India's first semi-high speed train Vande Bharat Express flagged off by Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**15th February 2019**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off India's first semi-high-speed train, the Vande Bharat Express, on February 15, 2019, at New Delhi railway station.
 
• The train ran on the New Delhi–Kanpur–Allahabad–Varanasi route, connecting Uttar Pradesh's Varanasi to the capital city.
 
• The train's top speed is 160 kilometres per hour. 
 
• some other facts about the Vande Bharat Express:
 
• The train was previously known as Train 18. 
 
• It was designed and manufactured by the Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai, which is owned by the government. 
 
• The train has two classes of accommodation: AC Executive Class and AC chair. 
 
• The train offers onboard catering with vegetarian and non-vegetarian meal options. 
 
• The train's coaches have wider windows with roller blinds, overhead racks for luggage, electric outlets, reading lights, CCTV cameras, automatic doors, bio-vacuum toilets, and sensor-based water taps.
